text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 decode tail latency SLO breached for /v1/generate (model=rwd-7b-ctr). Region: us-west-2. Window: last 5m. p95=1.2s (SLO=500ms) p99=3.1s (SLO=1s). Affected routes: streaming responses (chunked).

sara: oncall here, seeing it in the dashboard. any active deploys? can someone grab pprof/traces?

omar: I pushed a TRT/FlashAttention kernel update to the runtime pool ~25m ago (rollout staged). I’ll check the rollout state.

maria: customer-facing: a few customers reported stalled streams and reconnects. CS flagged 2 enterprise tenants with request timeouts.

incident-bot: Deploy history: runtime-kernel-rollout @ 1953215100 -> 1953216000 (gradual). 40% of nodes have new kernel.

jin: grabbing perf traces now. quick prometheus query for p95/p99: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(decode_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(decode_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
results show tail mass shifted >2x on nodes in pool runtime-pool-3.

leo: thinking this looks like a paging / compaction interaction. New TRT kernels changed madvise/mmap hints which affected our pinned memory and caused kernel page faults under high concurrency. saw minor increase in minor faults per second on those hosts.

omar: confirmed: dmesg on host gw-runtime-18 shows repeated PFN mapping messages around rollout time. snippet: 
```
[  12.345678] vm_fault: page allocation failure, order:0, mode:0x80
[  12.345689] rwd_infer: page fault in isolate
```

sara: impact assessment: are calls failing or just higher latency? any streaming stalls that require client reconnect?

maria: a few streams did stall and clients retried; no data loss but 5xxs spiked to 0.8% from baseline 0.02% for the affected tenants.

jin: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel change on nodes with the new kernel (fast but requires node-restart/cordon) 2) toggle runtime env to disable FlashAttention fast-path via RUNTIME_FLASHATTN=0 (hot config) 3) route traffic away from affected pool to fallback model variant (rwd-7b-cpu/quant)

omar: I can hot-toggle the env flag on autoscaler-managed pods to disable the fast-path while we investigate. That should avoid the madvise path triggering. Doing it now for runtime-pool-3.

omar: command I’m running: 
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/decode-runtime RUNTIME_FLASHATTN=0 --record
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/decode-runtime --selector=pool=runtime-pool-3
```

sara: do it, then scale up fallback capacity if needed. I'll patch routing to prefer pool-1/2.

leo: also recommend enabling vm.zone_reclaim or disable transparent huge pages on those hosts as a follow-up, but that needs infra approval.

incident-bot: Action logged: env toggle started by omar @ 1953217202.

omar: rollout restart started, pods terminating and coming back with RUNTIME_FLASHATTN=0.

jin: after toggle, p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 480ms within two minutes on pool-3. p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 920ms. Streaming stalls count decreased.

maria: customers updated: CS notified the two tenants on workaround and we offered priority opt-out to dedicated pool while we do full rollback.

sara: good. next steps: (A) keep disabled fast-path for 2h and observe; (B) schedule full node rollback of kernel change in staging then canary; (C) run kernel revert or recompile with different madvise flags and re-run our paging stress tests.

omar: opened GH issue linking kernel build id + compile flags and perf artifacts: https://go/rwd/issue/4129. I’ll collect flamegraphs and heap snapshots.

jin: handoff: I’m taking oncall for the next 60m to monitor. Sara, if anything escalates ping me. I’ll keep this thread updated.

sara: thanks. I'll be reachable if CS needs exec comms. removing page routing for pool-3 from automatic scale to avoid churn.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation applied (env toggle) @ 1953217420. p95 now 480ms, p99 920ms; SLO still borderline for p99 but trending down.

leo: long-term: we should add a preflight kernel/perf gate that runs our decode tail test under realistic batch/concurrency during kernel rollouts. filing follow-up doc.

maria: I'll draft customer incident note once we have full RCA.

jin: monitoring: kept a watch rule and increased sampling for traces on pool-1/3. leaving a small scrub script running to detect re-emergence of page faults.

sara: handoff accepted. I’ll check back in 30m for status and then sign out. Good work team. :thumbsup:
